quotes.text: Copilot isn't a search engine, and it's not a place you go to look up an answer someone else already wrote. It's a tool that writes alongside you in your file using the clues in front of it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates Copilot from a search engine and explains why its answers feel personal.

quotes.text: Copilot only knows what you show it. And this single idea explains almost every complaint people have about it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names context as the root cause of most disappointing Copilot results.

quotes.text: A practical way to think about it is that context is your steering wheel. The tool has plenty of power, and the context decides which direction that power goes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable metaphor for why context matters more than the tool's cleverness.

quotes.text: Use completion when you're mid-thought and you want momentum, use ask when you want to understand something before you touch it. Use edit when you know the exact change you want.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical rule of thumb for picking the right Copilot mode.

quotes.text: It speeds up people who can read what it produces, and it exposes people who can't. The tool raises your ceiling and it doesn't remove the floor.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up why Copilot is no replacement for understanding the code.

takeaways: GitHub Copilot is a prediction engine inside your editor that suggests and explains code, so every suggestion must be reviewed rather than trusted.
Use completion for momentum, ask mode to understand, edit mode for known changes, and agent mode only for multi-file jobs you are ready to review.
On personal plans your interactions can be used to improve models by default, so opt out and never paste secrets or client code.
hook: Many beginners think GitHub Copilot writes code for them and get burned by confident mistakes or a pile of unreviewed agent edits. This episode explains in plain language what Copilot is, how its three modes and context work, what the plans cost and how privacy and ownership work. Anyone who writes code, scripts or formulas will know when to reach for which mode and how to stay safe.
